newsitem.title: FINLAND: Partek up sharply but off peak on merger.
newsitem.headline: Partek up sharply but off peak on merger.

text.p: Shares in Finnish cargo handling equipment group Partek were sharply higher after the group said it would buy 51 percent of Swedish Kalmar Industries.
At 1320 GMT, Partek traded at 93.00 markka, up 3.20 markka or 3.6 percent, and trade was a moderate 8.5 million markka.
The share peaked briefly at 96.00 markka as trade resumed at 1310 GMT after suspension pending the annoucement.
"This was good news, so the direction is right, but I have not yet had time to figure out what the share should cost," one broker said.

An analyst agreed the news was good and said Metra's transfer of its lock unit to Swedish ASSA for a stake in the company showed that such Finnish-Swedish cooperation had worked before. He welcomed the projected synergies.
Partek said the merger would create the world's largest container handling equipment company and yield synergies worth some 65 million to 100 million markka per year.
"It is also good that the listing (of Kalmar) will be held, it will be a liquid asset," the analyst added.
